claims.text: A machine-learning potential incorporating ab initio liquid configurations will improve the representation of atomic interactions in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Improved representation by the machine-learning potential will increase reference–target phase-space overlap.
Increased reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The proposed method applies to both solid and liquid states near their high melting temperatures.
The proposed intervention is the development of a machine-learning potential trained with ab initio liquid configurations.
The proposed composition range comprises high-entropy alloys with three to six principal elements.
The proposed temperature range is 0.8 to 1.2 times the alloy melting temperature.
The machine-learning potential will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by 30% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Thermodynamic-integration path mismatch can be assessed using the free-energy difference between the reference and target systems.
TOR-TILD's EAM references are the baseline against which the proposed potential will be evaluated.
The accuracy of the proposed potential may be limited by the quality of its training data.
The proposed machine-learning method may have a higher computational cost than traditional EAM approaches.
The benchmark will compare free-energy calculations from the new potential and TOR-TILD EAM references against ab initio results for a set of high-entropy alloys.
The hypothesis is falsified if the new potential fails to reduce path mismatch by at least 20% relative to TOR-TILD EAM references for 80% of the tested alloys.
